newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila SEC gives free hand to IPO underwriters.
newsitem.headline: Manila SEC gives free hand to IPO underwriters.

text.p: The Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission said on Tuesday it was giving underwriters a free hand in distributing initial public offerings, scrapping a scheme that set aside a portion of IPOs to stockbrokers.

SEC chairman Perfecto Yasay said underwriters were no longer required to draw up specific rules for IPO distribution but directed that "they distribute the shares according to how much business a broker has."
Last week, the SEC issued a new memorandum which stopped the allocation of 15-50 percent of an IPO to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) to ensure wider distribution of shares.
The SEC said it believed the old system encouraged the hoarding of shares by brokers.
The memorandum required brokers to receive their IPO allocations from underwriters, not the PSE.

Brokers had complained the new system would not ensure the wider distribution of an IPO because it would remove the benefit of tapping the 177 active members of the exchange. It is also disadvantageous to brokers with no underwriting or investment house affiliations, analysts said.
